findings: Original mergeGroupList merges a group only if its first element is contained in the destination group. Synthetic A-B,B-C merges allthree without checking A-C; A-B,C-B remains two groups despite common B. It is anchor-dependent merging, not pairwise clique proof or guaranteed general connected-component computation.
Original expandGroupList emits query-to-member pairs only: A,B,C becomes A-B and A-C, not B-C. This matches needle-first group representation.

Original groupCompareByContents first checks equal lengths, makes a set only for the first group, then tests membership of every second-group path. It returns true for [A,B] vs[A,A], false in reverse. This qualifies generic test comparisons; no assertion that real scanner fixtures contain repeated paths.

Original Media operator< returns true for a< a when exactly MatchExact is set, violating irreflexivity expected by std::sort. Control invokes comparator directly; does not sort with that invalid relation or claim a reproduced crash. With combined flags exact-bit behavior differs because expression checks flags==MatchExact, not bit presence.

Media::setDefaults sets id0 and isValid checks id!=0. This closes previous default-Media uncertainty: a missing SQL row produces invalid Media and is excluded by Database::searchIndex. Tree-level tombstone control does not imply a displayed bogus item.

Header explicitly says md5 may exclude embedded JPEG metadata/tags. Database MD5 grouping therefore cannot be assumed byte-file equality even apart from hash-collision concerns. Actual checksum producer remains unread.
Media equality compares paths, not IDs/hashes/inode/content. Group merge membership and comparison inherit path identity; group naming does not establish duplicate-content identity.
